title.narrative: FISH-ADAPT: Transforming climate resilience and sustainability in Saint Lucia's fisheries communities

description.narrative:
1. The objective of this project is to develop climate resilient and sustainable fisheries in Saint Lucia for all fish landing sites around the island and shift the sector towards climate resilient pathway. The project is structured around three components presented below.
Component 1: Enhancement of the fisheries information management system. This component addresses the information barriers by disseminating and enhancing proven technologies and practices such as the system of data collection and analysis implemented under the readiness project, currently being prepared, and capacity building, including trainings on safety at sea being implemented in other Caribbean countries. The systems of data collection and analysis will be strengthened to include critical fisheries and aquaculture and expand socio-economic and other relevant climate change adaptation supporting information to enable more informed adaption planning, implementation and monitoring in the fisheries sector. This technology innovation is complemented with a co-management system for data collection involving fishing communities with the use of mobile applications. In component 1, GCF finances technical consultancies, the purchase of equipment to enhance the information management system in the fisheries sector and trainings. All activities in Component 1 are aligned with the Fisheries SASAP concept note 3- “Increasing the capacity of fishers and other actors to manage climate risks through improved data management and Early Warning Systems (EWS) “.
Sub-component 1.1[1]. Enhance theFisheries Statistics System based on the documentedproven integrated registries and advanced reporting platform utilisation.This sub-component will enhance and scale-up data collection and analysis systems on climate, productivity, livelihoods and other information that would support fishers and the government in planning, implementing and monitoring climate resilience measures in the fisheries sector. In sub-component 1.1, the project will strengthen and expand the localized Fisheries Statistics System from a limited number of landing sites in capture fisheries in Saint Lucia to a web-based and centralized information system for the whole country/fisheries. . Through scaling up synergistic project interventions in Saint Lucia and taking reference from information system that has been successfully tested and is being deployed in the small-scale fisheries context in Trinidad and Tobago, the project will strengthen access to climate information for climate-resilient fisheries in the Caribbean It will also mainstream data on fish aggregating devices (FAD) management, aquaculture and further socio-economic indicators including sex and age disaggregated data; training in data collection and management systems and; the validation and maintenance of the system with review of the statistics generated.Given the wider scope (nationwide system) of this initiative, linkages with the national statistical system will be made for robustness and sustainability
Sub-component 1.2.Enhancment of technical capacities of Saint Lucia Fisheries Department staff, fishers and fisherworkers in the use and analysis of gender sensitive data, climate-related information and statistics.Sub-component 1.2 focuses on reinforcing the technical capacities to improve access, collect and process climate-related information to improve the climate resilience of the fisheries sector in Saint Lucia. Lessons leant and experiences will be build on similar interventions at limited scale.
In this sub-component, staff members from the Fisheries Department will benefit from capacity building on fisheries socio-economic study and indicators[2]; collection of aquaculture data and statistical analysis; data analysis, including stock assessment and; reporting for national institutions, and regional and international organizations. Among others, the essential need of involving the primary fisheries resource users (and primarily affected by climate change impacts) in the data collection will be strengthened. This is justified by the fact that an important feature in this project is to enhance the involvement of fishers, fisherworkers and fishing communities in the data collection and feeding back to them the processed climate-related information. The regional dimension in the data reporting will also be addressed, given that Saint Lucia is an active member of several (sub) regional economic integration and resource management organizations that require data for sound decision making.
Sub-component 1.3. Strengthening the instruments to monitor impact of climate change on fisheries sector.Sub-component 1.3 supports the development of reporting tools for improving the information management system of the fisheries sector and the adoption of climate resilient measures. This will be achieved through the systematization and extension of the evaluation of fisheries sector value to all fisheries and aquaculture; the upgrade and implementation of the advanced dashboards and reporting tools, and training of the Department of Fisheries staff in the use of these dashboards. This sub-component is aligned to the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030)[3] as it contributes to understanding disaster risk; strengthening disaster risk governance to manage disaster risk; investing in disaster reduction for resilience and; enhancing disaster preparedness for effective response.
Sub-component 1.4. Production and dissemination of gender sensitive resilient-strengthening information for climate-resilient fisheries and dissemination of lessons learned.Sub-component 1.4 aim at ensuring an efficient interface between science and policy making, settin-up mechanisms for information to be able to influence policy-making. It finances the production and dissemination of relevant communication materials for awareness raising and dissemination of lessons learned from the implementation of the project activities. Activities include outreach workshops in the main fishers’ communities with all stakeholders to raise awareness of the importance of the data collection; develop communication materials on a yearly basis to inform the decision-makers and fisheries planners, private investors and fisherfolk and general public and; explore ways to properly utilize data and information for evidence-based policy-making and sector management. Activities include develop promotional material on defined topics like some other projects components (Use of Fisheries Aggregating Devices, awareness of the value of the overall sector value; the nutritional benefits of fish, safety at sea); streamline and institutionalize instruments for fisher communities to share their knowledge with the Department of Fisheries and; training of fisherfolks for the use of mobile applications for a co-management system of data collection.
Sub-component 1.5. Knowledge transfer and capacity building on safety at sea to inform fisherfolks on extreme weather events.Finally, sub-component 1.5 will provide better and updated climate information for fishers and train fishers to be able to respond to safety at sea information, building on smartphone and weather products that have been developed and successfully implemented in previous initiatives (see paragraph 12 and Annex 3). These priorities have been identified in Saint Lucia’s NAP, and were included in the Fisheries SASAP concept note 3- Increasing the capacity of fishers and other actors to manage climate risks through improved data management and Early Warning Systems (EWS)”. The activities include enhancing systems for accessing communications on climate forecasts safety at sea including additional hardware (radio transmitters) and operations; deliver formalized training and certification in understanding and responding to forecasts/safety at sea for fishers, and improve reporting systems, monitoring and climatic data collection from fishers.
Component 2. Implemented priority interventions to enhance the fisheries sector resilience to climate change.This component addresses each of the priority risks identified in Section B1 in turn, focusing on the assessment of gaps and solutions in the fisheries value chain and the identification and implementation of interventions to increase resilience to climate change by addressing the technical, information, financingand gender (special focus will be given on gender maintrainming, ensuring greater participation and benefit of women and youth in the sector) barriers. In component 2, GCF will finance technical consultancies, technical assistance, workshops and the purchase of equipment (such as radio transmitters and solar dryers). Co-finance from the Department of Fisheries will support the project with technical assistance, rooms for workshops and field schools as well as resources for travels to the communities. Activities will be implemented at the community and cooperatives level.
Sub-component 2.1. Implement climate-resilient aquaculture and resilient coastal livelihood diversification.This sub-component will involve the assessment of main gaps in the fisheries value chain as a whole and identification and implementation of solutions to increase resilience to climate change in the sector, involving all relevant stakeholders (including the `fisherfolk`communities, the government and private sector enterprises of the fisheries sector). This subcomponent aim at developing climate-resilient coastal aquaculture, supporting existing aquaculture farmers to address the changing climate, as well as developing the sector to provide more resilient livelihoods for coastal communities affected by climate change. It will include a range of activities for capacity building and access to resources (for the implementation of climate resilient practices) through field schools to increase climate resilience, with a priority given to women and youth. These are included in the NAP and Fisheries SASAP concept note 5- “Strengthening aquaculture and mariculture farming through diversification and business opportunities”. Under CC4FISH an Aquaculture Development and Management Plan was developed in consultation with stakeholders, to guide the development of aquaculture for the next five years. The activities include: assessing the fisheries value chain to identify the main gaps and possible solutions to increase the resilience to climate change; the development ofclimate resilient aquaculture field schools and curriculum activities, establishing demonstration sites in all fishing communities, including equipment for training; awareness raising and training, including it in national vocational standards for aquaculture at the aquaculture field schools; demonstration of solar dryers, targeting two highly vulnerable coastal communities; technical assistance for business plans and value chain development for a climate-resilient fisheries and aquaculture sector engaging relevant stakeholders involved in the sector (`fisherfolk`communities, the government and private sector enterprises); the development of a special planning framework to ensure that aquaculture operations stay within the carrying capacity of surrounding ecosystems, and the implementation of recirculating aquaculture systems such as aquaponics and the development and promotion of more efficient on farm water management systems.
Sub-component 2.2. Designing Climate Resilient Fisheries Infrastructure.There is a need to climate proof existing fisheries infrastructure to the changing climate, and ensure new upgrades and sites are climate resilient. This component will provide technical assistance to review the level of risk for current infrastructure and provide new designs for current and future infrastructure for rolling renewal. These activities are included in the Fisheries SASAP concept note 6- “Upgrading fisheries facilities to be more resilient to the impacts of climate change” (but this project does not include actual infrastructure construction). The activities include: climate resilient design for fishery facilities, including design standards, building codes and engineering plans; technical assistance to design a climate resilient upgrade of Castries fish landing site, and technical assistance to develop a business model to raise revenues for implementation of designs, as well as maintenance and future upgrade.
Component 3. Strengthened climate-resilient and gender sensitive fisheries policy and planning.This component will strengthen the institutional capacity and regulatory framework for mainstreaming climate change and achieve effective planning and responsive fisheries policy implementation. In component 3, GCF will finance technical consultancies, trainings and workshops while the Department of Fisheries will co-finance with technical assistance and travel expenses.
Sub-component 3.1. Strengthening climate mainstreaming capacity and integration in fisheries and aquaculture.This sub-component will strengthen institutional capacity to prepare for climate change in the fisheries and aquaculture sector and balance food security, adaptation and mitigation goals. It will support mainstreaming of climate resilience fisheries and aquaculture into the policy, regulatory and legal framework in Saint Lucia, to strengthen climate resilient approaches in future sector development planning. Considering the barriers identified above, special focus will be given on gender maintrainming, ensuring greater participation and benefit of women and youth in the sector. This will provide a framework to ensure the uptake of component 2 interventions in fisheries policies and plans, and provide a clear exit strategy for the project. Activities include: the production of training materials for integrating climate resilience into extension services, vocational training standards and quality control standards and; awareness raising and training using material produced in sub-component 1.4 for integrating climate change into extension services, vocational training standards and quality control standards.
Sub-component 3.2.Nationalmonitoring and adaptive learning as part of a Coastal Adaptation Blueprint.This sub-component will support national monitoring and evaluation and use of this in a learning-based adaptive management approach, including the establishment or strengthening of an appropriate mechanism for participatory monitoring and evaluation to facilitate learning by doing. It implements the coastal adaptation blueprint in theFisheries SASAP (concept note 9- “Coastal Adaptation Blueprint for Saint Lucia”)to ensure climate change evidence is integrated into future fisheries policy and planning. Activities include: technical assistance to integrate learning and use information in fisheries policy implementation planning, as part of adaptive mangagement to help address changing risks and; technical assistance in the monitoring and evaluation of the FAD management plan and connected socio-economic information.
2. A theory of change has been produced for the project, presented in Annex 4.
The anticipatedimpactis a climate resilient sector in Saint Lucia. The outcomes and outputs are:
Outcome 1) Stakeholders have access to adequate information to improve resilience to climate change in the fisheries sector:
Output 1. Information management system for adaptation measures planning, implementing and monitoring is improved:
· Improve information management system through equipment, training and knowledge sharing.
· Improve safety at sea through equipment, user awareness and training.
Outcome 2) Resilience to climate change is strengthened in fisheries sector:
Output 2. Priority climate resilient interventions to address major climate threats are implemented:
· Gaps and solutions to increase resilience in the fisheries value chain identified with stakeholders involved in the sector.
· Climate resilient practices taken up by fishers, through capacity building, knowledge and demonstration and pressure on ecosystems reduced,
· Disseminate climate resilient coastal aquaculture and resilient livelihoods through demonstration awareness and vocational standards,
· Design resilient coastal infrastructure and develop sustainable business models.
Outcome 3) Climate change is mainstreamed into fisheries policy and planning.
Output 3. Increased capacity for climate resilient planning and development:
· Institutional strengthening for climate responsive planning and mainstreaming,
· Strengthen staff technical capacity,
· Integrate climate resilient curriculum and activities in extension services,
· Use and link information and learning to inform future fisheries policy and plans.
3. The components outlined in this concept note have all undergone recent analysis and activities in Saint Lucia, funded under previous projects (as outlined in Annex 3). These have identified the potential for scaling up and transformative impacts (see also Annex 3), in specific high risk areas (safety at sea, resilient fisheries, and climate resilient aquaculture) and for mainstreaming climate change adaptation into fisheries planning and policy. All of the interventions have high benefit to cost ratios (See section B3 on efficiency and effectiveness).
4. The Accredited Entity is the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO). FAO has existing experience as an AE for GCF funded projects. FAO is already undertaking climate change adaptation activities in fisheries in the Eastern Caribbean and specifically in Saint Lucia. Success is further demonstrated from other countries (e.g. Grenada, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Trinidad and Tobago) which can be replicated in Saint Lucia. For example, in Grenada, the Climate Change Adaptation of the Eastern Caribbean Fisheries Sector Project (CC4FISH) is developing and implementing fisheries and emergency response training at the community level in order to improve disaster preparedness as well as improve recording of damages and losses of the fisheries sector in Post-Disaster Damage and Needs assessment. In Saint Kitts and Nevis, there has been implementation of aquaponics school systems which can improve linkages with youth and agriculture, and support learning and knowledge exchange as well as basic fishers training to improve resilience to climate change impacts. In Grenada, St. Kitts and Nevis and Trinidad and Tobago there has been extensive training in ICT for fisherfolk to improve safety at sea e.g training in use of VHF radios, GPS use and enhanced use of cellphones. FAO has successfully developed and implemented Fisheries Statistics and Management Information Systems - FISMIS (The Bahamas, Trinidad and Tobago; in progress for Suriname and Grenada) with a the support of the Fisheries Agency Japan and regional projects such as CC4FISH, REBYC II LAC and CLME+. The new FISMIS platform called Calipseo is instrumental to provide timely and reliable fisheries data and information as evidences of climate change impact on fisheries and to inform mitigation actions and policies. It also addresses the complexity of assessing small-scale fisheries sector. FAO has a team of statisticians and FISMIS experts with long standing experience in the region. The FAO has a dedicated high-quality project management unit, with expertise in all the relevant areas for project execution, including M&E, legal, administrative and finance, and effective project management. This unit has been operational for many years and has a demonstrated track record. FAO will also act as the project manager, including procurement activities, and thus carry out the executing role for the project.
Implementation arrangements
5. A project management unit (PMU) will be established within the Department of Fisheries of the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Physical Planning in Saint Lucia, which is the project Executing Entity. The project will be overseen by a Steering Committee. This will serve as the decision-making body and will review progress and evaluations, facilitate implementation and provide guidance. It will involve Government representatives from Ministries, Authorities and Agencies, including the NDA, the Department of Statistics and the UNFCCC Climate Focal Point. It will include representatives from private sector including cooperatives and small processing enterprises (described in annex 2), non-governmental and community-based organizations such as St. Lucia Fish Marketing Corporation, Lucian Blue Oceans, the Soufriere Marine Management Association and the St Lucia Fisherfolk Organization (SLFFO), etc. .) gender and community-based organizations and non-profit technical organizations like the Caribbean Natural Resources Institute (CANARI), UWI (CERMES and CIRP). The committee will be responsible for ensuring there is a strong gender balance and participation from identified vulnerable groups throughout the project.
6. This project builds on previous and ongoing projects (see section B.1 and Annex 3). It uses a professional international accredited entity as well as existing institutional arrangements and there is a high confidence on the project delivery and success. For these reasons, the risks to the implementation and execution are considered low. The FAO has existing protocols and guidance for financial and operational risk and these will be applied in the project.
7. The project will undertake M&E to ensure the project undertakes routine and concurrent monitoring, interim and final evaluations, and annual reports. As an international AE, the FAO will ensure all M&E is undertaken and reported using international best practice standards, including the use of independent evaluation teams.
